portName: Port of Copenhagen (Oceankaj, Langelinie, Nordre Toldbod)
seoTitle: Copenhagen cruise port guide: Oceankaj, Langelinie, Nyhavn
seoDescription: Copenhagen cruise port 2026: Langelinie is 5 min from the Little Mermaid; Oceankaj needs bus 25 or 164 plus metro M4, 24 kr. Rosenborg 140 kr online.
quickAnswer: Copenhagen has three cruise berths. From Langelinie and Nordre Toldbod you can walk to the Little Mermaid in about 5 minutes and on to Nyhavn; from Oceankaj in Nordhavn take bus 25 or 164 to Orientkaj and metro M4 to Kongens Nytorv, about 20 minutes on a 2-zone ticket (24 kr). Start back 75 minutes before you must be on board from Oceankaj, 45 minutes from Langelinie.
intro: Which quay your ship uses decides the day in Copenhagen. Langelinie and Nordre Toldbod are on the city's waterfront, minutes from the Little Mermaid, with Amalienborg and Nyhavn a pleasant walk south. Oceankaj, where most large ships now berth, is out in the Nordhavn container port and needs a bus and the metro. Once in the centre, everything is flat and close: Nyhavn's canal boats, Rosenborg's crown jewels, Christiansborg on its island and Tivoli by the central station. Copenhagen is also a major turnaround port, so on some days the terminals are busy with luggage and coaches rather than day visitors.

terminals.name: Oceankaj (Ocean Quay), Nordhavn
terminals.notes: The largest terminal and furthest from the centre, about 8 km by road and 25–30 minutes by car. Too far to walk to the metro (about 45 minutes). Buses 25 and 164 stop at the terminal and run to Orientkaj metro (M4); when ships are in, buses run every 10–20 minutes. Cruise lines may run a shuttle; check on board.

terminals.name: Langelinie
terminals.notes: On the waterfront next to the Little Mermaid (about 5 minutes on foot). Bus 27 runs from the Indiakaj stop, 5 minutes from the ships, to Østerport station; it usually runs only when cruise ships are in. Østerport is about 15 minutes' walk.

terminals.name: Nordre Toldbod
terminals.notes: Smallest and most central berth, just south of the Little Mermaid. About 10 minutes' walk along the water to Amalienborg and Nyhavn, and about 14 minutes to Marmorkirken metro (M3/M4). Harbour buses 991 and 992 stop nearby.

walkability.detail: From Langelinie: 5 minutes to the Little Mermaid, then south past Nordre Toldbod and along the water to Amalienborg and Nyhavn, all flat, about 25 minutes in total. From Nordre Toldbod it is about 10 minutes to Amalienborg or Nyhavn. From Oceankaj, walking is not practical: take the bus and metro or a taxi.

transportSections.time: About 20 min to Kongens Nytorv, 30 min to Central Station
transportSections.detail: Board bus 25 or 164 at the Oceankaj stop by terminal 1 to Orientkaj, the end of metro line M4, then ride M4 towards Kongens Nytorv for Nyhavn. One 2-zone ticket covers bus and metro together. Buy in the DOT Tickets/Rejsekort app, from metro machines or from the bus driver.

Walk 5 minutes to the Indiakaj stop. Bus 27 runs to Østerport station for metro M3/M4 and S-trains. Only buses ending at Langelinie serve the quay, and they usually run only on cruise days. Walking to Østerport takes about 15 minutes.

transportSections.time: About 14 min walk to Marmorkirken, then 1 stop to Kongens Nytorv
transportSections.detail: Marmorkirken is under 1 km from the quay. Most visitors simply walk along the water to Nyhavn instead.
Unlimited bus, metro, train and harbour bus travel in zones 1–4, including the airport. Worth it if you will make four or more trips. Sold in the apps and at station machines.

transportSections.cost: Normal public transport ticket (24 kr for 2 zones, 2026)
transportSections.time: Full route just over an hour
transportSections.detail: Commuter boats on the harbour between København Syd and Refshaleøen, with a stop near Nordre Toldbod. Line 991 runs south, 992 north. A cheap way to see the waterfront; tickets work across bus, metro and harbour bus.

transportSections.cost: Oceankaj to Kongens Nytorv about 175 kr by day, 215 kr evening; Langelinie to Kongens Nytorv about 96 kr by day (2026 estimates)
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait at the terminals. Fares are Visit Copenhagen's estimates and depend on traffic. Pay by card.
Stops at Langelinie and serves Nyhavn, Amalienborg and Tivoli.

returnTiming.rule: For Oceankaj, leave Kongens Nytorv 75 minutes before you must be on board (for a 17:30 all-aboard, by 15:15 to be on board by 16:30). For Langelinie or Nordre Toldbod, leave Nyhavn 45 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: The Oceankaj trip is about 20 minutes on the metro and bus plus waits: buses run every 10–20 minutes on ship days. From Nyhavn to Langelinie on foot is about 25 minutes.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi from a rank at Kongens Nytorv or Nyhavn: about 175 kr and 25 minutes to Oceankaj by day. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you will be late.

excursionAdvice: Copenhagen is easy to do alone, even from Oceankaj. A ship excursion is worth it mainly for trips outside the city, such as Kronborg Castle at Helsingør or Roskilde, where a coach saves connections, or for passengers with limited mobility at Oceankaj. For the city itself, the metro, a canal tour and your own feet cover the main sights for far less.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at Oceankaj at 08:00. From Langelinie, walk to the Little Mermaid and Nyhavn instead of taking the bus and metro.

steps.what: Bus 25 or 164 from the terminal to Orientkaj, then metro M4 to Østerport or Marmorkirken.
Walk past Kastellet to the Little Mermaid before the coach groups arrive.
Walk south along the water to Amalienborg. Stay for the changing of the guard at noon if you wish, or carry on.
Rosenborg Castle on a pre-booked timed ticket (about 1 hour), with a walk in the King's Garden.
Lunch at Torvehallerne food market by Nørreport.
Canal tour from Nyhavn (allow up to 2 hours including the queue).
Short walk around Nyhavn, then metro M4 from Kongens Nytorv to Orientkaj.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: The Little Mermaid
sights.why: The bronze statue from Hans Christian Andersen's tale, on the rocks at Langelinie.
sights.tip: Smaller than most people expect. Go early: by late morning coach groups crowd the shore.

sights.name: Nyhavn
sights.why: The 17th-century canal lined with coloured townhouses and old boats, and the start point for canal tours.
sights.tip: The quayside restaurants charge for the view; eat elsewhere and just walk it.

sights.name: Canal tour from Nyhavn
sights.why: The best way to see the harbour, Christianshavn and the Opera House in one go.
sights.timeNeeded: Allow up to 2 hours including the queue
sights.cost: Stromma from 135 kr online, 209 kr standard (2026)
sights.tip: Stromma's boats leave from Nyhavn 3 and Ved Stranden. Book online for the lower price.

sights.name: Rosenborg Castle
sights.why: A Renaissance royal castle with the Danish crown jewels in the Treasury, set in the King's Garden.
sights.cost: 140 kr online, 150 kr at the door; under-18s free (2026)
sights.tip: Entry is by timed slot every 10 minutes and slots sell out in summer, so book online. Open daily 10:00–17:00 until 1 November 2026; from 2 November closed Mondays. Nørreport station is about 200 m away.

sights.name: Christiansborg Palace
sights.why: The seat of the Danish parliament, with the Royal Reception Rooms, the medieval ruins beneath, the Royal Kitchen and Royal Stables.
sights.cost: Palace Ticket 215 kr online, 225 kr at the door; Royal Reception Rooms 140 kr online; under-18s free (2026)
sights.tip: On Slotsholmen, about 10 minutes' walk from Nyhavn. Buy online to save 10 kr per ticket.

sights.name: Amalienborg
sights.why: The four palaces of the royal family around an octagonal square, between Nordre Toldbod and Nyhavn.
sights.tip: The changing of the Royal Guard takes place at noon.

sights.name: Tivoli Gardens
sights.why: The 19th-century amusement park and gardens beside Central Station.
sights.cost: Charged; check tivoli.dk for the date you visit
sights.tip: Seasonal: Halloween runs 2 October–1 November 2026 and Christmas 13 November 2026–3 January 2027. The 2027 summer season runs 30 March–26 September 2027. Rides cost extra.

food.where: Pølsevogn sausage stands around the centre, e.g. near Kongens Nytorv

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming you can walk into town from Oceankaj.
commonMistakes.fix: It is about 45 minutes just to the metro. Take bus 25 or 164 to Orientkaj and metro M4.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at Rosenborg without a timed ticket in summer.
commonMistakes.fix: Book a slot online; it is cheaper (140 kr) and slots sell out.
Copenhagen's cycle lanes are busy and fast. Stay on the pavement and look both ways before crossing them.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning a summer Tivoli visit on an autumn or winter call.
commonMistakes.fix: Tivoli opens only in themed seasons; check the season dates before you plan around it.
Prices reflect the view. Torvehallerne or Reffen give better value.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying a 3-zone ticket for the city.
commonMistakes.fix: A 2-zone ticket (24 kr) covers any cruise terminal to central Copenhagen; 3 zones are needed only for the airport.

safety: Copenhagen is a safe city by day. Pickpockets work in crowded places: Nyhavn, Strøget, Central Station and on busy metro trains. The most common danger for visitors is cycle traffic: bike lanes run beside every main road and cyclists move fast. In an emergency call 112.
scams: Pickpocketing in crowds at Nyhavn, on Strøget and around Central Station. Keep bags zipped and phones out of back pockets.
Street 'shell games' on or near Strøget, where onlookers in the crowd are part of the act. Do not play.
Overpriced food and drinks on the Nyhavn quayside. Check the menu prices before you sit down.
accessibility: Copenhagen is flat and most pavements are smooth, which makes the Langelinie–Little Mermaid–Nyhavn walk manageable for most people. From Oceankaj, the bus and metro route works for wheelchair users, but a taxi is simpler. Rosenborg has no lift: wheelchair users can see only the ground floor and the Treasury, with help on the steps. Cobbles around Nyhavn and Amalienborg are uneven.
rainyDay: Rosenborg and Christiansborg are both mostly indoors and close to the metro. Torvehallerne's glass halls are a dry place for lunch. A covered canal boat still works in light rain.
crowdTips: The Little Mermaid is busiest from about 10:00 to 14:00, when coach groups stop there, so go early or late. Nyhavn and the canal-tour queues peak around midday. Rosenborg limits entry with timed slots that sell out in summer. On turnaround days the terminals are busy with arrivals and departures; leave extra time at Oceankaj.

faqs.q: Is Copenhagen cruise port walkable to the city?
faqs.a: From Langelinie and Nordre Toldbod, yes: the Little Mermaid is about 5 minutes away and Nyhavn about 25 minutes from Langelinie. From Oceankaj, no: take the bus and metro.

faqs.q: How do I get from Oceankaj to Nyhavn?
faqs.a: Take bus 25 or 164 from the terminal to Orientkaj, then metro M4 to Kongens Nytorv, next to Nyhavn. About 20 minutes on a 2-zone ticket, 24 kr (2026).

faqs.q: Does bus 27 go to the cruise terminal?
faqs.a: Bus 27 serves Langelinie, from the Indiakaj stop 5 minutes from the ships to Østerport station, and usually runs only on cruise days. For Oceankaj, use buses 25 or 164.
No. Ships dock at Oceankaj, Langelinie or Nordre Toldbod.

faqs.q: Is Tivoli open when my ship calls?
faqs.a: Only in its seasons. In 2026, Halloween runs 2 October–1 November and Christmas from 13 November to 3 January 2027. The 2027 summer season runs 30 March–26 September.
140 kr online or 150 kr at the door; under-18s free (2026). Entry is by timed slot.

faqs.q: What can I do in Copenhagen in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Little Mermaid, Amalienborg, Rosenborg, lunch at Torvehallerne and a canal tour from Nyhavn. All on foot and by metro.

faqs.q: Is Copenhagen safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes. Watch for pickpockets in crowded areas and for cyclists when crossing bike lanes.
